shared_text:
The flight. An airliner on final approach to an airport before dawn, cleared for a visual approach.

The crew. The first officer was the pilot flying and the captain the pilot monitoring.

What happened. Approach control had the aircraft at 3,000 ft, gave it a heading to intercept the final approach course, and shortly afterwards cleared it for a visual approach. The crew were backing up the visual approach with the instrument landing system approach to the same runway. When the autopilot captured the localiser, the aircraft did not appear to be turning towards the approach path. The captain said that it looked like a false capture and that the first officer would have to hand-fly the approach. The first officer concentrated on not overshooting the final approach course. The aircraft was on the segment of the approach that is shown at 2,000 ft. The first officer descended to about 1,700 ft before the captain pointed out the altitude deviation, and the first officer promptly began to correct. As the first officer was correcting, the enhanced ground proximity warning system gave one aural "Pull up" warning.
safe_outcome: After the correction, the first officer flew the aircraft to a stable approach and landed. There was no conflict with other traffic. No one was hurt and the aircraft was not damaged.
bad_outcome: Another aircraft was descending nearby. Both crews received TCAS resolution advisories and followed them, and the aircraft passed about 300 feet vertically and half a mile apart. A flight attendant on this aircraft was thrown against a galley cart during the manoeuvre and received a minor injury.

notes: Single narrative (first officer, pilot flying); the report has no reflection section. Rule 3: 'slightly fixated on ensuring we don't overshoot final' replaced by the stated intent, 'concentrated on not overshooting the final approach course'. The synopsis wording 'failed to intercept' is not used. Rule 5, moved to the safe ending: the stable approach and landing. Rule 6: airport, runway, flight number and the 080 heading removed. Judgement calls: aircraft type is not reported ('Commercial Fixed Wing'), so 'an airliner' rather than one of the brief's classes. Light is not coded; 'before dawn' is inferred from the coded local time (00:01-06:00, January). Bracket 'descending': the aircraft was near the final approach course, where other arriving traffic would be descending.
